answer:
Analyze a cantilever beam of length L = 1800 mm, fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L.
Use N–mm–MPa units and Euler–Bernoulli beam theory (small deflection, linear elastic).
The beam is structural steel with E = 200000 MPa and constant second moment of area I = 1200000 mm^4.
A downward point load P = 2000 N is applied at the free end.
The bending moment varies linearly from PL at the fixed end to 0 at the free end.
Ignore the earlier statements about zero free-end rotation and constant moment PL, as those were errors.
Determine the slope at the free end as θ = PL² / (2EI).
Determine the vertical deflection at the free end as δ = PL³ / (3EI).
Report the slope in radians (optionally also in degrees) and the deflection in mm, with downward deflection noted.
Expected results: θ = 0.0135 rad (≈ 0.773°) and δ = 16.2 mm downward.
